46:1: Surah Al-Ahqaf It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty informs us that He sent down the Book to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, forever until the Day of Judgment. He described Himself with unparalleled glory and wisdom in words and deeds. Then God the Almighty said: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth meaning not in vain or falsehood. And for a specified term meaning for a specific fixed period that neither increases nor decreases. And His statement: And those who disbelieve turn away from that of which they are warned meaning there is no weakness in what is intended for them. God the Almighty sent down a Book to them and sent a Messenger to them, but they turn away from all of that, meaning they will come to know after that. Then God the Almighty said: Say meaning to these polytheists who worship other than God, Have you seen what you invoke besides God? Show me what they have created on the earth meaning guide me to the place on earth that they independently created. Or do they have a share in the heavens? They have no partner in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they possess even a speck of dust. Indeed, the sovereignty and control all belongs to God, the Almighty, the Majestic. So how can you worship other than Him and associate others with Him? Who guided you to this? Who called you to it? Did He command you to do it? Or is it something you suggested of your own selves? That is why He said: Bring me a book before this meaning bring a book from the books of God revealed to the prophets peace be upon them, commanding you to worship these idols or a trace of knowledge meaning clear evidence for this path that you have taken if you should be truthful meaning you have no evidence, neither transmitted nor rational, for that. That is why others read: or a trace of knowledge meaning or correct knowledge that you transmit from someone before you, as Mujahid said about His statement: or a trace of knowledge or someone who transmits knowledge. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: or clear evidence of the matter. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salim, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Sufyan said: I do not know except from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, or a trace of knowledge, he said: handwriting. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: Or a remnant of knowledge. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Or a trace of something that he extracts and stirs up. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, and Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also said: Or a trace of knowledge, meaning handwriting. Qatadah said: Or a trace of knowledge specifically from knowledge. All of these sayings are close to each other. They go back to what we have said, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, honor him, and grant him a good abode. God the Almighty said: And who is more astray than he who invokes besides God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware. That is, there is no one more astray than he who invokes idols besides God, and asks for what they cannot do until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of what he says; they do not hear, see, or strike, because they are inanimate, deaf stones. God the Almighty said: And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will disbelieve in their worship. Like His statement: “And they have taken other than God deities that might be for them a means of honor. No! They will deny their worship and will be opponents to them.” That is, they will betray them when they are most in need of them. Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “You only took idols besides God out of affection among yourselves in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will disbelieve in one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.”

46:7: God the Almighty says, informing about the polytheists in their disbelief and stubbornness: That when the clear verses of God are recited to them, that is, when they are made clear, evident, and evident, they say, This is obvious magic, that is, obvious magic, and they have lied, fabricated, gone astray, and disbelieved. Or do they say, ‘He invented it,’ meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? God the Almighty says: Say, ‘If I invented it, then you will not possess for me anything against God.’ That is, if I lied about him and claimed that he sent me, when he was not, then He would punish me with the most severe punishment, and no one on earth, neither you nor anyone else, would be able to protect me from him, as God the Blessed and Exalted says: Say, ‘No one can protect me from God, and I will not find besides Him a refuge,* Except by conveying [the message] from God and His messages.’ And God the Almighty says: “And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, * We would have seized him by the right hand, * Then We would have cut from him the aorta, * And there is not one of you who could prevent Him from Him.” That is why God the Almighty says here: “Say, ‘If I have invented it, then you do not possess for me anything against God. He is most knowing of what you conceal. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you.’” This is a clear threat, a warning, and a severe intimidation. And the saying of God the Almighty: And He is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful is an encouragement to them to repent and return to Him, meaning that despite all of this, if you return and repent, He will accept your repentance, pardon you, forgive you, and have mercy. This verse is like the saying of God the Almighty in Surat al-Furqan 25:“And they say, ‘Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.’ Say, ‘It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.’” And the saying of God the Almighty: Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ Meaning, I am not the first messenger to come to the world, rather messengers came before me, so I am not something that has no equal for you to find me strange and reject my mission to you, for God the Almighty sent all the prophets to the nations before me. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Mujahid, and Qatadah said, Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ Meaning, I am not the first messenger. Neither Ibn Jarir nor Ibn Abi Hatim narrated anything other than that. And the saying of God the Almighty: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both regarding this verse: After it was revealed: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. And this is what Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It was abrogated by the saying of God the Almighty: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. They said: When this verse was revealed, a Muslim man said: God the Almighty has made this clear. What will He do with you, O Messenger of God, so what will He do with us? So God the Almighty revealed: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow. This is what he said. What is established in the Sahih is that the believers said: Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God, but what will be with us? So God the Almighty revealed this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, meaning I do not know what I am commanded to do and what He forbade after this. Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding the verse: {And I do not know what will be done with me or with you} He said: As for the Hereafter, God forbid! He knew that he would be in Paradise, but he said: I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world. Will I be brought out as the prophets before me were brought out? Or will I be killed as the prophets before me were killed? And I do not know whether the earth will swallow you up or you will be pelted with stones? This is the statement that Ibn Jarir relied on and no other is permissible. There is no doubt that this is what is appropriate for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because with regard to the Hereafter he was certain that he and those who followed him would go to Paradise. As for this world, he did not know what the outcome of his situation and the situation of the polytheists of Quraysh would be: Will they believe or disbelieve and be punished and uprooted because of their disbelief. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit, on the authority of Umm Al-Ala, one of their women, who told him and who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: When the Ansar drew lots for the residence of the Muhajireen, they had a choice between Uthman bin Mazun, may God be pleased with him. Uthman, may God be pleased with him, fell ill with us, so we nursed him until he died. We wrapped him in his garments, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us. I said, May God have mercy on you, Abu Al-Sa’ib, my testimony to you is that God, the Almighty, has honored you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, And how do you know that God, the Almighty, has honored him? I said, I do not know, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By God, I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what will be done to me.” She said: By God, I will never vouch for anyone after him, and that saddened me. Then I slept and saw a flowing spring for Uthman, may God be pleased with him. I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is his work. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, not Muslim. In another version of his, he said: “I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what will be done to him.” This is more likely to be the correct version, based on her statement, That saddened me. This and similar hadiths indicate that no one is certain of Paradise except those whom the Lawgiver has specifically designated, such as the ten, Ibn Salam, Al-Ghumaysa, Bilal, Suraqa, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir, the seventy reciters who were killed at Bir Ma’unah, Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja’far, Ibn Rawahah, and others like them, may God be pleased with them. His statement, I only follow what is revealed to me, means I only follow what God sends down to me of revelation. And I am only a clear warner, meaning that my warning is clear and apparent to every person of reason and intellect. And God knows best.

God the Almighty says: Say, ‘If I invented it, then you will not possess for me anything against God.’ That is, if I lied about him and claimed that he sent me, when he was not, then He would punish me with the most severe punishment, and no one on earth, neither you nor anyone else, would be able to protect me from him, as God the Blessed and Exalted says: Say, ‘No one can protect me from God, and I will not find besides Him a refuge,* Except by conveying [the message] from God and His messages.’ And God the Almighty says: “And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, * We would have seized him by the right hand, * Then We would have cut from him the aorta, * And there is not one of you who could prevent Him from Him.” That is why God the Almighty says here: “Say, ‘If I have invented it, then you do not possess for me anything against God. He is most knowing of what you conceal. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you.’” This is a clear threat, a warning, and a severe intimidation. And the saying of God the Almighty: And He is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful is an encouragement to them to repent and return to Him, meaning that despite all of this, if you return and repent, He will accept your repentance, pardon you, forgive you, and have mercy. This verse is like the saying of God the Almighty in Surat al-Furqan 25:“And they say, ‘Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.’ Say, ‘It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.’” And the saying of God the Almighty: Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ Meaning, I am not the first messenger to come to the world, rather messengers came before me, so I am not something that has no equal for you to find me strange and reject my mission to you, for God the Almighty sent all the prophets to the nations before me. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Mujahid, and Qatadah said, Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ Meaning, I am not the first messenger. Neither Ibn Jarir nor Ibn Abi Hatim narrated anything other than that. And the saying of God the Almighty: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both regarding this verse: After it was revealed: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. And this is what Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It was abrogated by the saying of God the Almighty: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. They said: When this verse was revealed, a Muslim man said: God the Almighty has made this clear. What will He do with you, O Messenger of God, so what will He do with us? So God the Almighty revealed: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow. This is what he said. What is established in the Sahih is that the believers said: Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God, but what will be with us? So God the Almighty revealed this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, meaning I do not know what I am commanded to do and what He forbade after this. Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding the verse: {And I do not know what will be done with me or with you} He said: As for the Hereafter, God forbid! He knew that he would be in Paradise, but he said: I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world. Will I be brought out as the prophets before me were brought out? Or will I be killed as the prophets before me were killed? And I do not know whether the earth will swallow you up or you will be pelted with stones? This is the statement that Ibn Jarir relied on and no other is permissible. There is no doubt that this is what is appropriate for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because with regard to the Hereafter he was certain that he and those who followed him would go to Paradise. As for this world, he did not know what the outcome of his situation and the situation of the polytheists of Quraysh would be: Will they believe or disbelieve and be punished and uprooted because of their disbelief. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit, on the authority of Umm Al-Ala, one of their women, who told him and who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: When the Ansar drew lots for the residence of the Muhajireen, they had a choice between Uthman bin Mazun, may God be pleased with him. Uthman, may God be pleased with him, fell ill with us, so we nursed him until he died. We wrapped him in his garments, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us. I said, May God have mercy on you, Abu Al-Sa’ib, my testimony to you is that God, the Almighty, has honored you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, And how do you know that God, the Almighty, has honored him? I said, I do not know, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By God, I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what will be done to me.” She said: By God, I will never vouch for anyone after him, and that saddened me. Then I slept and saw a flowing spring for Uthman, may God be pleased with him. I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is his work. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, not Muslim. In another version of his, he said: “I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what will be done to him.” This is more likely to be the correct version, based on her statement, That saddened me. This and similar hadiths indicate that no one is certain of Paradise except those whom the Lawgiver has specifically designated, such as the ten, Ibn Salam, Al-Ghumaysa, Bilal, Suraqa, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir, the seventy reciters who were killed at Bir Ma’unah, Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja’far, Ibn Rawahah, and others like them, may God be pleased with them. His statement, I only follow what is revealed to me, means I only follow what God sends down to me of revelation. And I am only a clear warner, meaning that my warning is clear and apparent to every person of reason and intellect. And God knows best.

46:10: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who disbelieve in the Qur’an, Have you considered if this Qur’an is from God and you disbelieve in it? That is, what do you think God would do to you if this Book that I have brought to you was sent down to me so that I could convey it to you, and you have disbelieved in it and denied it? And a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it. That is, the previous scriptures sent down to the prophets before me, peace and blessings be upon them, have testified to its truthfulness and authenticity. They gave glad tidings of it and informed of the same as this Qur’an has informed of. And the words of God the Almighty: So he believed meaning this is the one who testified to his truthfulness from the Children of Israel because of his knowledge of his reality and you were arrogant about following him. Masruq said: So this witness believed in his prophet and his book and you disbelieved in your prophet and your book Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people This witness is a generic name that includes Abdullah ibn Salam may God be pleased with him and others, for this verse was revealed in Mecca before the conversion of Abdullah ibn Salam may God be pleased with him to Islam. This is like the words of God the Almighty: "And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims in submission." And He said: "Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them - fall upon their chins in prostration * And say, 'Exalted is our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'" Masruq and Ash-Sha'bi said: This verse is not about Abdullah ibn Salam, and the conversion of Abdullah ibn Salam may God be pleased with him to Islam was in Medina. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from them, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Malik said, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, on the authority of Amir ibn Sa`d, on the authority of his father, who said: I never heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about anyone walking on the face of the earth that he was from the people of Paradise, except for `Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him. He said: And it was concerning him that the verse, And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it was revealed. Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Malik with this chain of transmission. This is also what Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, `Ikrimah, Yusuf ibn `Abdullah ibn Salam, Hilal ibn Yasaf, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, Malik ibn Anas, and Ibn Zayd said, that they all said that he was `Abdullah ibn Salam. God the Almighty says: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ That is, they said about the believers in the Qur’an, If the Qur’an had been good, these people would not have preceded us to it. They mean Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, and Khabbab may God be pleased with them, and those like them and similar to them from among the weak, male and female slaves. This is only because they believe in themselves that they have standing with God and that He cares for them. They made a grave mistake in that and made a clear error, as God the Almighty said: And thus We have tried some of them by means of others that they may say, ‘Are these among us whom God has favored?’ That is, they wonder how these people were guided and not us. For this reason they said, If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. As for Ahl as-Sunnah wa’l-Jama’ah, they say: Every action and statement that has not been proven from the Companions may God be pleased with them is an innovation, because if it had been good, they would have preceded us to it, because they did not leave out a single good characteristic without hastening to do it. God the Almighty says: And when they are not guided by it meaning the Qur’an they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood’ meaning an ancient lie, that is, one passed down from ancient people, thus belittling the Qur’an and its people. This is the arrogance about which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Then God the Almighty says: And before it was the Scripture of Moses meaning the Torah “as a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book” meaning the Qur’an confirming meaning the Scriptures that came before it in an Arabic tongue meaning eloquent, clear and explicit to warn those who do wrong and as good tidings to the doers of good meaning it contains a warning to the disbelievers and good tidings to the believers. God the Almighty says: So there will be no fear concerning them meaning in what is to come nor will they grieve for what will come after them Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as reward for what they used to do meaning deeds are a reason for mercy to be attained and bestowed upon them, and God knows best.

Malik said, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, on the authority of Amir ibn Sa`d, on the authority of his father, who said: I never heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about anyone walking on the face of the earth that he was from the people of Paradise, except for `Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him. He said: And it was concerning him that the verse, And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it was revealed. Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Malik with this chain of transmission. This is also what Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, `Ikrimah, Yusuf ibn `Abdullah ibn Salam, Hilal ibn Yasaf, al-Suddi, al-Thawri, Malik ibn Anas, and Ibn Zayd said, that they all said that he was `Abdullah ibn Salam. God the Almighty says: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ That is, they said about the believers in the Qur’an, If the Qur’an had been good, these people would not have preceded us to it. They mean Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, and Khabbab may God be pleased with them, and those like them and similar to them from among the weak, male and female slaves. This is only because they believe in themselves that they have standing with God and that He cares for them. They made a grave mistake in that and made a clear error, as God the Almighty said: And thus We have tried some of them by means of others that they may say, ‘Are these among us whom God has favored?’ That is, they wonder how these people were guided and not us. For this reason they said, If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. As for Ahl as-Sunnah wa’l-Jama’ah, they say: Every action and statement that has not been proven from the Companions may God be pleased with them is an innovation, because if it had been good, they would have preceded us to it, because they did not leave out a single good characteristic without hastening to do it. God the Almighty says: And when they are not guided by it meaning the Qur’an they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood’ meaning an ancient lie, that is, one passed down from ancient people, thus belittling the Qur’an and its people. This is the arrogance about which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Then God the Almighty says: And before it was the Scripture of Moses meaning the Torah “as a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book” meaning the Qur’an confirming meaning the Scriptures that came before it in an Arabic tongue meaning eloquent, clear and explicit to warn those who do wrong and as good tidings to the doers of good meaning it contains a warning to the disbelievers and good tidings to the believers. God the Almighty says: So there will be no fear concerning them meaning in what is to come nor will they grieve for what will come after them Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as reward for what they used to do meaning deeds are a reason for mercy to be attained and bestowed upon them, and God knows best.
46:14: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who disbelieve in the Qur’an, Have you considered if this Qur’an is from God and you disbelieve in it? That is, what do you think God would do to you if this Book that I have brought to you was sent down to me so that I could convey it to you, and you have disbelieved in it and denied it? And a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it. That is, the previous scriptures sent down to the prophets before me, peace and blessings be upon them, have testified to its truthfulness and authenticity. They gave glad tidings of it and informed of the same as this Qur’an has informed of. And the words of God the Almighty: So he believed meaning this is the one who testified to his truthfulness from the Children of Israel because of his knowledge of his reality and you were arrogant about following him. Masruq said: So this witness believed in his prophet and his book and you disbelieved in your prophet and your book Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people This witness is a generic name that includes Abdullah ibn Salam may God be pleased with him and others, for this verse was revealed in Mecca before the conversion of Abdullah ibn Salam may God be pleased with him to Islam. This is like the words of God the Almighty: "And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims in submission." And He said: "Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them - fall upon their chins in prostration * And say, 'Exalted is our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'" 46:15: When God, the Almighty, mentioned in the first verse the Oneness of God, the sincerity of worship and righteousness to Him, He followed it with the commandment to be kind to parents, as is mentioned in more than one verse in the Quran, such as His statement, “And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. And to parents, good treatment.” And His statement, the Most High, the Majestic, “That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination.” And there are many other verses like that. And God, the Almighty, said here, And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment. That is, We have commanded him to be kind to them and compassionate towards them. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, Shu’bah narrated to us, Simak ibn Harb informed me, saying: I heard Mus’ab ibn Sa’d narrating on the authority of Sa’d, may God be pleased with him, who said: Umm Sa’d said to Sa’d, Has not God commanded us to obey our parents? I will not eat food or drink anything until you disbelieve in God, the Almighty. So she abstained from food and drink until they began to open her mouth with a stick, and this verse was revealed, And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment. It was narrated by Muslim and the Sunan scholars, except Ibn Majah, on the authority of Shu’bah, with a chain of transmission similar to it but longer than it. His mother carried him with difficulty, meaning she suffered from the pain and fatigue of carrying him, such as morning sickness, nausea, heaviness, distress, and other fatigue and hardship that pregnant women suffer. And she gave birth to him with difficulty, meaning also with difficulty and intensity from the contractions. And his gestation and weaning lasted thirty months. Ali may God be pleased with him used this verse, along with the verse in Luqman 31:And his weaning is in two years, and the words of God the Most High: Mothers may breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever desires to complete the nursing, as evidence that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. This is a strong and correct inference, and Uthman and a group of the Companions may God be pleased with them agreed with him on this. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ubaydullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Muammar ibn Abdullah al-Juhani, who said: A man among us married a woman from Juhayna, and she gave birth to him after six months. Her husband went to Uthman may God be pleased with him and mentioned that to him. He sent for her, and when she got up to put on her clothes, her sister cried, so she said: What makes you cry? By God, no one among God’s creation has ever confused me with him, and God, the Exalted, decrees as He wills. When she was brought to Uthman may God be pleased with him, he ordered that she be stoned. report of that reached Ali may God be pleased with him, so he came to him and said to him, What are you doing? He said, “I gave birth at six months. Is that possible?” Ali may God be pleased with him said to him, Do you not read the Quran? He said, Yes. He said, Haven’t you heard God, the Almighty, say, ‘And his gestation and weaning is thirty months,’ and He said, ‘Two complete years.’ But we did not find that there were only six months left. Uthman may God be pleased with him said, “By God, I did not realize this. Bring the woman to me.” They found that she had been finished with him. Muammar said, By God, neither a crow nor an egg is more similar to an egg than he is to his father. When his father saw him, he said, My son, by God, I do not doubt him. God, the Almighty, tested him with this eaten sore on his face, and it continued to eat at him until he died. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and we have mentioned it from another chain of transmission when God, the Almighty, said, Then I am the first of the worshippers. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra told us, Ali ibn Masahr told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: If a woman gives birth after nine months, then breastfeeding her for twenty-one months is sufficient. If she gives birth after seven months, then breastfeeding her for twenty-three months is sufficient. If she gives birth after six months, then breastfeeding her for two full years, because God the Almighty says: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months until he reaches his full strength meaning he becomes strong, mature, and mature. And reaches forty years meaning his mind is mature and his understanding and patience are complete. It is said that he usually does not change from what he is at forty. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abd Al-Rahman, who said: I said to Masruq: When will a man be held accountable for his sins? He said: When you reach forty, then be on your guard. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Abu Abdullah al-Qawariri told us, Urwah ibn Qays al-Azdi told us, and he had reached the age of one hundred. Abu al-Hasan al-Saluli Umar ibn Aws told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Uthman said, on the authority of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a Muslim servant reaches the age of forty, God Almighty makes his account easy. When he reaches the age of sixty, God Almighty grants him repentance to Him. When he reaches the age of seventy, the people of heaven love him. When he reaches the age of eighty, God Almighty confirms his good deeds and erases his bad deeds. When he reaches the age of ninety, God forgives his past and future sins. God Almighty accepts his intercession for his family, and he is written in heaven as a prisoner of God on His earth.” This has been narrated from more than one source, and it is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. Al-Hajjaj ibn Abdullah al-Hakami, one of the princes of the Umayyads in Damascus, said: I abandoned sins and wrongdoings for forty years out of shyness before people, then I abandoned them out of shyness before God Almighty. How beautiful is the saying of the poet: He kept on drinking until his hair turned white. When it turned white, he said to falsehood: Go away! “He said, ‘My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You will approve’ in the future, ‘and make righteous for me my offspring’ in the future, ‘I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.’” This is guidance for those who have reached the age of forty to renew their repentance and return to God, the Almighty, and to be determined to do so. Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to teach them to say in the tashahHud 11:“O God, unite our hearts and reconcile our differences, guide us to the paths of peace and save us from darkness into light and keep us away from immoralities, both apparent and hidden, and bless our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses and our offspring, and accept our repentance, for You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful. Make us grateful for Your favor, praising You for it, accepting it and completing it for us.” God, the Almighty, said: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, among the companions of Paradise. That is, these are they. Those who are described as we mentioned, those who repent to God Almighty and turn to Him, who make up for what they missed through repentance and seeking forgiveness, are those from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their bad deeds, so We forgive them many of their mistakes and accept from them the little of their deeds. Among the companions of Paradise meaning they are among the companions of Paradise, and this is their judgment before God, as He has promised to those who repent and turn to Him. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: The promise of truth which they were promised. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told me, Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Al-Ghatrif, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, on the authority of the Trustworthy Spirit, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: “The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant will be brought and they will be recompensed for one another. If one good deed remains, God, the Most High, will expand Paradise for him.” He said: So I went to Yazid and he narrated something similar to this. He said: I said: What if the good deed is lost? He said: “Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. They are among the companions of Paradise, the promise of truth which they were promised.” And this is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd Al-A’la Al-San’ani, on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, with a similar chain of transmission, and he added, on the authority of the Trustworthy Spirit. He said: The Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, said: The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant will be brought, and he mentioned it. It is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is good and there is nothing wrong with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sulayman ibn Ma'bad told us, Amr ibn Asim al-Kila'i told us, Abu 'Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyya, on the authority of Abu Wahshiyya, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Sa'd, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: He stayed in my house when Ali may God be pleased with him defeated the people of Basra. One day he said to him: I witnessed the Commander of the Faithful Ali may God be pleased with him, and with him were Ammar, Sa'sa'a, al-Ashtar, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr may God be pleased with them. They mentioned Uthman may God be pleased with him and spoke ill of him. Ali may God be pleased with him was on the bed with a stick in his hand. One of them said: You have someone who will judge between you. They asked him, and Ali may God be pleased with him said: Uthman may God be pleased with him was among those about whom God the Most High said: "Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. They are among the companions of Paradise - a promise of truth which they were promised." He said: By God, Uthman and the companions of Uthman may God be pleased with them. He said it three times. Yusuf said: I said to Muhammad ibn Hatib: By God, I heard this from Ali may God be pleased with him? He said: By God, I heard this from Ali, may God be pleased with him.

46:17: When God the Almighty mentioned the state of those who supplicate for their parents and what success and salvation they have with Him, He linked it with the state of the wretched who are disobedient to their parents, saying: And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you both!’ This is general in meaning for everyone who says this. And he is free from it and says: I fear that I will be like those to whom God said, rebuked and rebuked: You spent your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them. That is, to turn us away from our gods, Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful. They hastened the punishment and chastisement of God, ruling out its occurrence, as God Almighty said, Those who do not believe in it hasten it. “He said, ‘Knowledge is only with God.’” That is, God knows best about you. If you deserve to hasten the punishment, then He will do that to you. As for me, it is my business to convey to you what I was sent with. But I see that you are a people who are ignorant. That is, you do not reason or understand. God the Almighty said: {But when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys} meaning, when they saw the torment approaching them, they believed that it was a rain-bearing cloud, so they rejoiced and were glad about it, although they were destitute and in need of rain. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Hubab narrated to us, Abu Al-Mundhir Salam bin Sulaiman Al-Nahwi narrated to us, he said: Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud narrated to us, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Harith Al-Bakri, he said: I went out to complain to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about Al-Ala’ bin Al-Hadrami. I passed by Ar-Rabdhah, and there was an old woman from Banu Tamim who was stranded there. She said to me: O servant of God, I have a need from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), will you deliver it to him? So I carried her and went to Madinah. There was the mosque crowded with its people, a black banner was waving, and Bilal may God be pleased with him was holding his sword in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said: What is the matter with the people? They said: He wants to send Amr bin Al-Aas may God be pleased with him as a commander. So I sat down and he entered his house, or he said his tent, and I asked permission to enter and he gave me permission. So I entered and greeted him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Was there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. I passed by an old woman from Banu Tamim who was isolated. She asked me to carry her to you, and here she was at the door. So he gave her permission and she entered. I said: O Messenger of God, if you see that you should put a barrier between us and Tamim, then make it Ad-Dahna. The old woman became angry and said: O Messenger of God, where will your needy be forced to go? He said: I said, the likes of me, as the first one said, are goats that carry their death. I carried this one and I do not feel that she was an opponent to me. I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the delegate of Ad. He said: And what is the delegate of Ad? He is more knowledgeable about Hadith than him, but he finds it enjoyable. I said: The tribe of ‘Aad suffered a drought, so they sent a delegation called Qil. They passed by Mu’awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, giving him wine to drink and singing to him were two girls called Al-Jaradatayn. When the month had passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahrah and said: O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a captive to benefit him. O God, give ‘Aad water as You used to give them water. Black clouds passed by him, and a voice was called from one of them, Choose. He pointed to one of the black clouds, and a voice was called from it, “Take it, black ashes. Leave no one of ‘Aad alone.” When I heard that a wind was sent against them, except for the amount that runs through this ring of mine, until they perished, Abu Wa’il said: He spoke the truth. When a man or a woman sent a delegation, they would say: Do not be like the delegation of ‘Aad. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, as mentioned above in Surat Al-A’raf. Imam Ahmad said: Harun bin Maruf told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr told us that Abu An-Nadr told him on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that she said: I never saw the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) laughing so much that I could see his uvula. He was only smiling. She said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw a cloud or a wind, you could see it in his face. She said: O Messenger of God, when people see a cloud, they rejoice in the hope that it will rain, and when I see you, I can see dislike in your face. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: O Aisha, what assures me that there is no punishment in it? Some people were punished with a wind, and some people saw the punishment and said, This is a cloud that will bring us rain. And they both narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Shuraih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw something emerging in a horizon of the sky, he would leave his work even if he was praying, then he would say: O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil in it. If God Almighty removed it, he would praise God Almighty, and if it rained, he would say: O God, make it a beneficial rain. Another chain of transmission Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr al-Tahir told us, Ibn Wahb told us: I heard Ibn Jurayj telling us on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “When the wind blew, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say: ‘O God, I ask You for its good and the good within it and the good with which You sent it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil within it and the evil with which You sent it.’ She said: ‘And when the sky became cloudy, his color would change, and he would go out and come in, come and go, and go back and forth. When it rained, he would be relieved. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, knew that, so she asked him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Perhaps, O Aisha, it is as the people of ‘Aad said: “But when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’” We have already mentioned the story of the destruction of the people of ‘Aad in Surat al-A’raf and Surat Hud, so there is no need to repeat it here. To God be praise and thanks. Al-Tabarani said: Abdun bin Ahmad told us, Ismail bin Zakariya Al-Kufi told us, Abu Malik bin Muslim Al-Mala’i told us, on the authority of Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Nothing was opened to the ‘Ad tribe from the wind except the size of a ring. Then the Bedouins were sent against them to the cities. When the people of the cities saw it, they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain, approaching their valleys,’ and the people of the desert were among them. So the people of the desert attacked the people of the cities until they perished. He said, ‘It rebelled against its treasurers until it came out through the doors.’ And God Almighty knows best.”

She said to me: O servant of God, I have a need from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), will you deliver it to him? So I carried her and went to Madinah. I said: What is the matter with the people? They said: He wants to send Amr bin Al-Aas may God be pleased with him as a commander. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Was there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. 46:26: God Almighty says: “And We had already established the previous nations in this world with wealth and children, and We gave them from it what We have not given you the like of or anything close to it. And We gave them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and sight and hearts availed them nothing when they denied the signs of God, and that which they used to ridicule encompassed them.” That is, the torment and punishment that they used to deny and rule out happening encompassed them. So beware, O you who are being addressed, lest you be like them, lest you be afflicted with the same torment that afflicted them in this world and the hereafter. God the Almighty says: {And We have certainly destroyed the towns around you} meaning the people of Mecca. God also destroyed the nations that denied the messengers around Mecca, such as Aad, who were in Al-Ahqaf in Hadramaut near Yemen, and Thamud, whose homes were between them and Ash-Sham, and the same for Saba, who were the people of Yemen, and Madyan, which was on their way and passage to Gaza, and the same for the lake of the people of Lot, who also passed by it. God the Almighty says: {And We have diversified the signs} meaning We explained them and made them clear, {that perhaps they might return. * Then why did not those whom they took as deities other than God aid them} meaning did they aid them when they were in need of them? {Rather, they have gone astray from them} meaning they have departed from them when they were in dire need of them. {And that is their falsehood} meaning their lie, {and what they used to invent} meaning their fabrication in taking them as deities. They failed and lost in their worship of them and their reliance on them, and God knows best.

46:29: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, Amr told us, I heard Ikrimah from Az-Zubayr, And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. He said: In Nakhl, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying the last ‘Isha’ prayer. They were almost covered over him like felt, one over the other. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. It will come from the narration of Ibn Jarir from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that they were seven from the jinn of Nasibin. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Awana told us H and the famous Imam, the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said in his book, Dala’il al-Nubuwwah: Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Ahmad Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubayd al-Saffar told us, Ismail al-Qadi told us, Musaddad told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite to the jinn nor did he see them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, intending to go to the market of Ukaz, and the devils had been prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors had been sent upon them. The devils returned to their people and said, What is wrong with you? They said, We have been prevented from receiving report from heaven. So they set out, striking the east and west of the earth, seeking what had prevented them from receiving report from heaven. Then those people who had headed towards Tihamah turned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Nakhalah, heading for the market of Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur’an, they listened to it and said: This, by God, is what has come between you and the report from heaven. So when they returned to their people, they said: “Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’an. It guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate with our Lord anyone.” And God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened.” And what was revealed to him was the words of the jinn. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Musaddad in a similar manner, and Muslim narrated it from Shaiban bin Farukh from Abu ‘Awanah with it, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the interpretation from the hadith of Abu ‘Awanah. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Ahmad told us, Isra’il told us from Abu Ishaq from Sa’id bin Jubayr from Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The jinn would listen to the revelation, and they would hear a word and add ten to it, so what they heard would be true and what they added would be false. The stars were not thrown before that, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, no one of them would come to his seat except that he was thrown by a meteor that burned whatever it hit, so they complained about that to Satan, and he said: This is nothing but something that has happened, so he sent out his soldiers and there they found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying between two palm trees, so they came to him and told him, and he said: This is the story that happened on earth, and Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it in their two books of interpretation from their Sunan from the hadith of Israel with it, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic, and thus Ayoub narrated it on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and likewise Al-Awfi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, also with a similar chain of transmission in full, and thus Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know about their matter until God, the Most High, revealed to him the report of them, and Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi the story of the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, departure to Taif and his supplication to God, the Almighty, and their refusal to him, so he mentioned the story in full and included that beautiful supplication: O God, to You I complain of my weakness and lack of strength. My trick and my humiliation among people, O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Most Merciful of the merciful, and You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To an enemy who oppresses me, or to a close friend to whom You have given authority over my affairs? If You are not angry with me, then I do not care, but Your well-being is more spacious for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your face by which the darkness is illuminated and by which the affairs of this world and the hereafter are put right, lest Your anger descend upon me or Your wrath befall me. To You is the reproach until You are satisfied, and there is no power or strength except with You. He said: When he left them, he spent the night in Nakhalah, reciting from the Qur’an that night, and the jinn of Nasibin listened to him. This is correct, but his statement that the jinn listened that night is questionable, because the jinn listened at the beginning of the revelation, as indicated by the aforementioned hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. And his departure, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Taif was after the death of his uncle, and that was one or two years before the Hijrah, as stated by Ibn Ishaq and others, and God knows best. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: They descended upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting the Qur’an in Batn al-Nakhal. “And when they attended it, they said, ‘Listen.’ He said, ‘Shh!’ And they were nine, and one of them was Zuba’ah. So God Almighty revealed: “And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. And when they attended it, they said, ‘Listen.’ And when it was concluded, they turned back to their people as warners.” This, along with the first narration of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, requires that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He did not feel their presence this time, but they listened to his recitation and then returned to their people. Then after that, they came to him in groups, one group after another and one group after another, as will come in the report of its place and the traces of what we will mention, God willing, and in Him we trust. As for what was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim together on the authority of Abu Qudamah Ubayd God ibn Saeed Al-Sarkhasi, on the authority of Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, on the authority of Misa’ar ibn Kadam, on the authority of Ma’n ibn Abd Al-Rahman, who said: I heard my father say: I asked Masruq, “Who informed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night when they listened to the Qur’an?” He said: Your father, meaning Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, told me that a tree informed him of them. It is possible that this was the first time and that it is an affirmation that precedes the denial of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. It is possible that it was the first time, but he did not notice them while they were listening until the tree informed him of them, that is, it informed him of their gathering. And God knows best. It is possible that this was on some of the later occasions, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi said: What Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, narrated was the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they knew his condition. At that time, he did not recite to them nor did he see them. Then after that, a caller from the jinn came to him and he recited the Qur’an to them and called them to God Almighty, as narrated by Abdullah Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Abi Za’idah, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Alqamah, who said: I said to Abdullah bin Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him: Did any of you accompany the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Night of the Jinn? He said: None of us accompanied him, but we missed him one night in Mecca, so we said: Was he assassinated? Brought to life? What did he do? He said: So we spent the worst night that a people had spent. When it was the break of dawn - or he said - in the early hours of the morning, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira. We said: O Messenger of God, and they mentioned to him what they had been through. He said: A caller of the jinn came to me, so I went to them and recited to them. He said: So he went and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. Al-Sha’bi said: They asked him for provisions. Aamer said: They asked him in Mecca and they were from the jinn of the peninsula. He said: Every bone on which the name of God has been mentioned that falls into your hands will have more meat, and every dung or excrement is fodder for your animals. He said: Do not use them for cleaning yourself, for they are the provisions of your brothers from the jinn. Muslim narrated it in this way in his Sahih on the authority of Ali ibn Hujr on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah with a similar wording. Muslim also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud - who is Ibn Abi Hind - told us on the authority of Amir, who said: I asked Alqamah: Was Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him present with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Night of the Jinn? Alqamah said: I asked Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him and said: Was any of you present with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Night of the Jinn? He said: No, but we were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one night and we missed him. We looked for him in the valleys and ravines, and it was said: Was he taken captive? Was he assassinated? He said: So we spent the worst night ever spent by any people. When morning came, he came from the direction of Hira. He said: We said: O Messenger of God, we missed you and looked for you but did not find you. We spent the worst night ever spent by any people. He said: A caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with them and recited the Qur’an to them. He said: So he set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provisions, and he said: Every bone on which the name of God has been mentioned that falls into your hands will have more meat, and every dung or excrement will be fodder for your animals. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not use them for cleaning yourself, for they are the food of your brothers. Another chain of transmission On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Ahmad bin Abd al-Rahman told me, my uncle told me, Yunus told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abdullah, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I spent the night reciting to the jinn while standing in al-Hujun. Another chain of transmission states that he was with him on the night of the jinn. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, my uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Uthman ibn Sunnah al-Khuza’i, who was from the people of Ash-Sham, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions while he was in Mecca: Whoever among you would like to be present during the affair of the jinn tonight, let him do so. None of them were present except me. He said: So we set off until we were at the top of Mecca. He drew a line for me with his foot, then ordered me to sit in it. Then he set off until he stood up and began to recite the Qur’an, but a great many black clouds covered him and stood between me and him until I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of clouds, going away until only a group of them remained. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished and gave them bones and dung, then he forbade anyone from using dung or bones to perfume themselves. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Wahb ibn Rashid, on the authority of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, with this chain of transmission. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Al-Dala’il from the hadith of Abdullah bin Saleh, the scribe of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yunus, on his authority. Ishaq bin Rahawayh narrated it from Jarir, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Al-Hafiz Abu Na’im narrated it from the path of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu’alla, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and he also mentioned something similar to it. Another chain of transmission Abu Naim said: Abu Malik told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told me, he said: Affan and Ikrimah told us, they said: Mu’tamir told us, he said: My father told me, Abu Tamima told me, on the authority of Amr, and perhaps al-Bakali said, Amr told him, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed me, so we set out until we came to such and such a place, and he drew a line for me and said: Stay in the back of this place and do not leave it, for if you leave it, you will perish. So he mentioned the hadith in full, and it contains great strangeness. Another chain of transmission Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Ghailan ath-Thaqafi, that he said to Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: I was told that you were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. He said: Yes. He said: How was it? Then he mentioned the hadith and mentioned that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) drew a line over him and said: Do not leave it. Then he mentioned something like a black cloud that overwhelmed the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and he was frightened three times until it was close to dawn. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to me and said: Are you asleep? I said: “No, by God. I thought many times of calling for help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your staff, saying: “Sit down.” Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If you went out, I would not be safe from some of them snatching you away. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Did you see anything? I said: Yes, I saw black men with white hair, wearing white clothes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Those were jinn from Nasibin who asked me for provisions - and provisions are provisions - so I gave them provisions with every loose bone, dung or excrement. I said: O Messenger of God, what will that do for them? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They will not find a bone without finding its flesh on it on the day it was eaten, nor dung without finding its seeds in it on the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself when he comes out of the toilet with a bone, dung or excrement.” Another way Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sammali and Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, he said: Abu Muhammad bin Yahya bin Mansour Al-Qadi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bushanji told us, Ruh bin Salah told us, Musa bin Ali bin Rabah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a follower and said: A group of fifteen jinn, sons of brothers and cousins, will come to me tonight so that I may recite the Qur’an to them. So I went with him to the place he wanted, and he drew a line for me and made me sit there and said to me: Do not leave this place. So I spent the night there until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me with magic in his hand, a broken bone, dung, and a birthmark, and he said: If you go to the toilet, do not clean yourself with anything of these. He said: When morning came, I said: “I will know where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was.” So I went and saw a place where sixty camels would kneel. Another chain of transmission Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Al-Abbas bin Muhammad Al-Duri informed us, Uthman bin Omar informed us, on the authority of Al-Shammar bin Al-Rayyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: I set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn until we reached Al-Hujun. He drew a line for me, then he advanced towards them, and they crowded around him. A chief of theirs, called Wardan, said: I will make them leave you. He said: No one will protect me from God. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan ibn Abi Fazarah al-Absi told us, Abu Zayd, the freed slave of Amr ibn Harith, told us, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the night of the jinn came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you have water with you? I said: I do not have water with me, but I have a jug of wine with me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A good date and pure water. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Zayd. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Qais ibn al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Hanash al-San’ani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them, who said: He was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, do you have water with you? He said: I have wine in a water skin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pour it over me. So he performed ablution. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, a drink and purification. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this chain of transmission. Ad-Daraqutni included it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, my father told me, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. When he had finished, he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. This is how I saw it in the Musnad in an abbreviated form. Al-Hafiz Abu Nu’aym narrated it in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, and he said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, and Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, my father told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Abu Bakr. He was silent, then a while passed, then he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Umar. He was silent for a while, then he passed away. Then he took a deep breath, so I said, What is the matter with you? He said, My death has been reported to me. I said, Then appoint a successor. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Who? I said, Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if they obey him, they will all enter Paradise, all of them. This is a very strange hadith and it is more likely that it has not been preserved. Assuming its authenticity, it appears that this was after their arrival to him in Medina, as we will mention, God willing. At that time, at the end of the matter, when Mecca was conquered and the people and the jinn also entered the religion of God in multitudes, the Surah “When the help of God and the conquest come, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance” was revealed. This is the Surah in which his noble soul was announced to him, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, stated, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, agreed with him on it. A hadith has been reported about that, which we will mention, God willing, when interpreting it. And God knows best. Abu Nu`aym also narrated it on the authority of Al-Tabari, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Husayn bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of Yahya bin Sa`id Al-Aslami, on the authority of Harb bin Subaih, on the authority of Sa`id bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Murrah Al-San`ani, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Jadali on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, mentioned it and mentioned the story of the succession. This is a strange chain of transmission and a wondrous context. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line around him, and one of them was like the blackness of a palm tree, and he said: Do not move from your place, and teach them the Book of God. When he saw the pasture, he said: They are like these. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you have water with you? I said: No. He said: Do you have wine with you? I said: Yes. So he performed ablution with it. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told us, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, he said: They were twelve thousand who came from the island of Mosul. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him: Give me time until I come to you, and he drew a line over it and said: Do not move until I come to you. When Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, feared them, he was about to leave, but he remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not move. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: If you had left, we would not have met until the Day of Resurrection. Another chain of transmission also transmitted: Sa`id bin Abi `Aruba said on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were directed to him from Nineveh and that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to recite to the jinn, so which of you will follow me? So they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him, and they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him a third time. A man said: O Messenger of God, that is the one with a scar, so Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, the brother of Hudhayl, followed him. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a valley called the Valley of al-Hujun and drew a line over it, and he drew a line over Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, to confirm it. He said: So I began to tremble and I saw things like eagles walking in their tambourines, and I heard a loud noise until I feared for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited the Qur’an, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, I said: O Messenger of God, what was the noise that I heard? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They disputed over a murdered person, and a judgment was passed between them in truth. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. All these methods indicate that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the jinn intentionally, recited the Qur’an to them, called them to God Almighty, and God Almighty prescribed for them through his tongue what they needed at that time. It may be possible that the first time they heard him recite the Qur’an, he did not notice them, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said. Then after that, they came to him, as narrated by Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him. As for Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him, he was not with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he addressed the jinn and called upon them. Rather, he was far away from him, and no one went out with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) except him. Despite this, he did not witness the speech. This is the method of Al-Bayhaqi. It may be possible that the first time he went out to them, neither Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him nor anyone else was with him, as is apparent in the context of the first narration on the authority of Imam Ahmad, which is in Muslim. Then after that, he went out with him another night, and God knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his interpretation of Say, ‘It has been revealed to me’ from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: `Abd Al-`Aziz ibn `Umar said: As for the jinn whom they met at Nakhlah, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn whom they met in Mecca, they were the jinn of Nasibin. Al-Bayhaqi interpreted it as meaning that he said, “We spent the worst night that a people spent, other than Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him who did not know about his (blessings and peace of God be upon him) going out to the jinn.” This is a remote possibility, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Amr Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Adeeb told us, Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili told us, Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Amr bin Yahya told us, on the authority of his grandfather Saeed bin Amr, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, used to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a vessel for his ablution and for his needs. One day he caught up with him and said, Who is this? He said, I am Abu Hurairah. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Bring me stones to clean myself with, but do not bring me bones or dung. So I brought him stones in my garment and placed them beside him. When he had finished and stood up, I followed him and said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with bones and dung? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A delegation of the jinn of Nasibin came to me and asked me for provisions, so I supplicated to God for them that they would not pass by a bone or dung without finding it to be food. Narrated by Al-Bukhari in his Sahih on the authority of Musa ibn Isma’il on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya with a similar chain of transmission. This indicates what was mentioned above, that they came to him after that, and we will mention, God willing, what indicates the repetition of that. Ibn Abbas narrated other narrations than what was narrated from him at first, from a new chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani narrated to us, Al-Nadr bin Arabi narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the verse: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed them as messengers to their people. This indicates that he narrated both stories. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein narrated to us, Suwaid bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, a man whom he named, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin, and their names were Huyy, Hasi, Mansa, Sasir, Nasir, Al-Ardubian, and Al-Ahtam. Abu Hamza Al-Thamali mentioned that this clan of jinn was called Banu Al-Shisaan, and they were the most numerous and noblest of the jinn, and they were the majority of Satan’s soldiers. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, that they were nine, one of them was Zuba`ah.
