Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Did you see anything? I said: Yes, I saw black men with white hair, wearing white clothes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Those were jinn from Nasibin who asked me for provisions - and provisions are provisions - so I gave them provisions with every loose bone, dung or excrement. I said: O Messenger of God, what will that do for them? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They will not find a bone without finding its flesh on it on the day it was eaten, nor dung without finding its seeds in it on the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself when he comes out of the toilet with a bone, dung or excrement.” Another way Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sammali and Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, he said: Abu Muhammad bin Yahya bin Mansour Al-Qadi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bushanji told us, Ruh bin Salah told us, Musa bin Ali bin Rabah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a follower and said: A group of fifteen jinn, sons of brothers and cousins, will come to me tonight so that I may recite the Qur’an to them. So I went with him to the place he wanted, and he drew a line for me and made me sit there and said to me: Do not leave this place. So I spent the night there until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me with magic in his hand, a broken bone, dung, and a birthmark, and he said: If you go to the toilet, do not clean yourself with anything of these. He said: When morning came, I said: “I will know where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was.” So I went and saw a place where sixty camels would kneel. Another chain of transmission Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Al-Abbas bin Muhammad Al-Duri informed us, Uthman bin Omar informed us, on the authority of Al-Shammar bin Al-Rayyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: I set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn until we reached Al-Hujun. He drew a line for me, then he advanced towards them, and they crowded around him. A chief of theirs, called Wardan, said: I will make them leave you. He said: No one will protect me from God. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan ibn Abi Fazarah al-Absi told us, Abu Zayd, the freed slave of Amr ibn Harith, told us, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the night of the jinn came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you have water with you? I said: I do not have water with me, but I have a jug of wine with me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A good date and pure water. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Zayd. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Qais ibn al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Hanash al-San’ani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them, who said: He was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, do you have water with you? He said: I have wine in a water skin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pour it over me. So he performed ablution. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, a drink and purification. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this chain of transmission. Ad-Daraqutni included it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, my father told me, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. When he had finished, he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. This is how I saw it in the Musnad in an abbreviated form. Al-Hafiz Abu Nu’aym narrated it in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, and he said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, and Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, my father told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Abu Bakr. He was silent, then a while passed, then he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Umar. He was silent for a while, then he passed away. Then he took a deep breath, so I said, What is the matter with you? He said, My death has been reported to me. I said, Then appoint a successor. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Who? I said, Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if they obey him, they will all enter Paradise, all of them. This is a very strange hadith and it is more likely that it has not been preserved. Assuming its authenticity, it appears that this was after their arrival to him in Medina, as we will mention, God willing. At that time, at the end of the matter, when Mecca was conquered and the people and the jinn also entered the religion of God in multitudes, the Surah “When the help of God and the conquest come, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance” was revealed. This is the Surah in which his noble soul was announced to him, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, stated, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, agreed with him on it. A hadith has been reported about that, which we will mention, God willing, when interpreting it. And God knows best. Abu Nu`aym also narrated it on the authority of Al-Tabari, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Husayn bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of Yahya bin Sa`id Al-Aslami, on the authority of Harb bin Subaih, on the authority of Sa`id bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Murrah Al-San`ani, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Jadali on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, mentioned it and mentioned the story of the succession. This is a strange chain of transmission and a wondrous context. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line around him, and one of them was like the blackness of a palm tree, and he said: Do not move from your place, and teach them the Book of God. When he saw the pasture, he said: They are like these. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you have water with you? I said: No. He said: Do you have wine with you? I said: Yes. So he performed ablution with it. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told us, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, he said: They were twelve thousand who came from the island of Mosul. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him: Give me time until I come to you, and he drew a line over it and said: Do not move until I come to you. When Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, feared them, he was about to leave, but he remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not move. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: If you had left, we would not have met until the Day of Resurrection. Another chain of transmission also transmitted: Sa`id bin Abi `Aruba said on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were directed to him from Nineveh and that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to recite to the jinn, so which of you will follow me? So they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him, and they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him a third time. A man said: O Messenger of God, that is the one with a scar, so Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, the brother of Hudhayl, followed him. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a valley called the Valley of al-Hujun and drew a line over it, and he drew a line over Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, to confirm it. He said: So I began to tremble and I saw things like eagles walking in their tambourines, and I heard a loud noise until I feared for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited the Qur’an, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, I said: O Messenger of God, what was the noise that I heard? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They disputed over a murdered person, and a judgment was passed between them in truth. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. All these methods indicate that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the jinn intentionally, recited the Qur’an to them, called them to God Almighty, and God Almighty prescribed for them through his tongue what they needed at that time. It may be possible that the first time they heard him recite the Qur’an, he did not notice them, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said. Then after that, they came to him, as narrated by Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him. As for Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him, he was not with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he addressed the jinn and called upon them. Rather, he was far away from him, and no one went out with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) except him. Despite this, he did not witness the speech. This is the method of Al-Bayhaqi. It may be possible that the first time he went out to them, neither Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him nor anyone else was with him, as is apparent in the context of the first narration on the authority of Imam Ahmad, which is in Muslim. Then after that, he went out with him another night, and God knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his interpretation of Say, ‘It has been revealed to me’ from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: `Abd Al-`Aziz ibn `Umar said: As for the jinn whom they met at Nakhlah, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn whom they met in Mecca, they were the jinn of Nasibin. Al-Bayhaqi interpreted it as meaning that he said, “We spent the worst night that a people spent, other than Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him who did not know about his (blessings and peace of God be upon him) going out to the jinn.” This is a remote possibility, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Amr Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Adeeb told us, Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili told us, Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Amr bin Yahya told us, on the authority of his grandfather Saeed bin Amr, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, used to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a vessel for his ablution and for his needs. One day he caught up with him and said, Who is this? He said, I am Abu Hurairah. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Bring me stones to clean myself with, but do not bring me bones or dung. So I brought him stones in my garment and placed them beside him. When he had finished and stood up, I followed him and said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with bones and dung? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A delegation of the jinn of Nasibin came to me and asked me for provisions, so I supplicated to God for them that they would not pass by a bone or dung without finding it to be food. Narrated by Al-Bukhari in his Sahih on the authority of Musa ibn Isma’il on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya with a similar chain of transmission. This indicates what was mentioned above, that they came to him after that, and we will mention, God willing, what indicates the repetition of that. Ibn Abbas narrated other narrations than what was narrated from him at first, from a new chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani narrated to us, Al-Nadr bin Arabi narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the verse: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed them as messengers to their people. This indicates that he narrated both stories. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein narrated to us, Suwaid bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, a man whom he named, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin, and their names were Huyy, Hasi, Mansa, Sasir, Nasir, Al-Ardubian, and Al-Ahtam. Abu Hamza Al-Thamali mentioned that this clan of jinn was called Banu Al-Shisaan, and they were the most numerous and noblest of the jinn, and they were the majority of Satan’s soldiers. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, that they were nine, one of them was Zuba`ah. They came to him from the base of a palm tree. It was mentioned earlier that they were fifteen, and in a narration that they were on sixty camels. It was mentioned earlier that the name of their master was Wardan, and it was said that they were three hundred. It was mentioned earlier on the authority of `Ikrimah that they were twelve thousand. Perhaps this difference is evidence of the repetition of their delegation to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. What indicates that is what al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn Wahb told me, `Umar told me, he is Ibn Muhammad, he said: Salim told him, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I never heard `Umar, may God be pleased with him, say anything, I think it is like this, except that it was as he thought. While `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was sitting, a handsome man passed by him and he said: My assumption was wrong, or This man is following his religion in the pre-Islamic period, or “He was their soothsayer. Bring me the man.” So he was summoned, and he said that to him. He said: I have never seen a Muslim man like today. He said: I urge you to do nothing but tell me. He said: I was… Their priest in the pre-Islamic period said: How strange is what your jinn brought you? He said: While I was in the market one day, she came to me and I knew she was frightened, and she said: Have you not seen the jinn and their despair and hopelessness after their defeat? And its pursuit of the camels and their saddles Umar may God be pleased with him said: He spoke the truth while I was sleeping beside their gods when a man came with a calf and slaughtered it. A caller cried out over it in a voice I had never heard a louder than his, saying: O Jalih, the order of Nujayh is an eloquent man who says: There is no god but God. The people jumped up and I said: I will not leave until I know what is behind this. Then he called: O Jalih, the order of Nujayh is an eloquent man who says: There is no god but God. I got up and it was not long before it was said: This is a prophet. This is the context of Bukhari. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb in a similar manner. Then he said: The apparent meaning of this narration suggests that Umar may God be pleased with him himself heard the caller crying out from the slaughtered calf. This is also clear in a weak narration from Umar may God be pleased with him. All the other narrations indicate that this soothsayer is the one who reported that he saw and heard it. And God knows best. What Al-Bayhaqi said is the correct one and this man is Sawad ibn Qarib. I have mentioned this in detail in the biography of Umar may God be pleased with him, so whoever wants it can take it from there. Praise and gratitude be to God. Al-Bayhaqi said: The hadith of Sawad bin Qarib, and it is likely that this is the soothsayer whose name was not mentioned in the authentic hadith, Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Habib al-Mufassir told us from the original hearing, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Asbahani told us, reading to him, Abu Ja`far Ahmad bin Musa al-Himar al-Kufi told us in Kufa, Ziyad bin Yazid bin Badawayh told us, Abu Bakr al-Qasri told us, Muhammad bin al-Nawwas al-Kufi told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara` may God be pleased with him, who said: While `Umar bin al-Khattab may God be pleased with him was delivering a sermon to the people on the pulpit of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said: O people, is Sawad bin Qarib among you? He said: No one answered him that year. Then the following year came, he said: O people, is Sawad bin Qarib among you? I said: O Commander of the Faithful, and who is Sawad bin Qarib? He said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said to him: The beginning of Sawad bin Qarib’s conversion to Islam was something amazing. He said: While we were like that, Sawad bin Qarib appeared. He said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said to him: O Sawad, tell us about the beginning of your conversion to Islam, how was it? Sawad, may God be pleased with him, said: I was staying in India and I had a vision from the jinn. He said: While I was sleeping one night, that came to me in my dream. He said: Get up and understand and reason if you can reason. A messenger has been sent from Lu’ay bin Ghalib. Then he began to say: I was amazed at the jinn and their feelings, and the camels’ attraction to their saddles. You go to Mecca seeking guidance. The jinn are not as good as its filth. Rise up to the elite of Hashim and look up to her head He said: Then he woke me up and startled me and said, O Sawad bin Qarib, God Almighty has sent a prophet, so rise up to him and you will be guided and be given the right direction. Then, on the second night, he came to me and woke me up and then began to say: I was amazed at the jinn and their demands, and the camels pulling them with their saddlebags. She heads to Mecca seeking guidance, her feet not like her tails Rise up to the elite of Hashim and look up to its summit Then, on the third night, he came to me, woke me up, and said: I was amazed at the jinn and their stories, and the camels pulling them with their camels She goes to Mecca seeking guidance. The evil ones are not like the good ones. Rise up to the elite of Hashim. The believers of the jinn are not like their disbelievers. He said: When I heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam, through the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell into my heart as God willed. He said: So I went to my saddlebag and tied it to my mount. I did not undo nine knots or tie another knot until I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and behold, he was in Medina, meaning Mecca, and the people were upon him like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw me, he said: “Welcome, O Sawad bin Qarib. We know what brought you.” He said: I said, O Messenger of God, I have recited poetry, so hear it from me. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say, O Sawad. So I said: A vision came to me after a long night of sleep, and it was not a liar among what I have been tested with. Three nights, saying every night: A messenger from Luay ibn Ghalib has come to you. So I rolled up my trousers and the foxes walked between the two sides of the river. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are trustworthy with all who are absent. You are the closest of the messengers to intercede with God, O son of the most noble and good. So command us to do what comes to you, O best messenger, even if what comes is gray hair. And be my intercessor on the day when there is no intercessor but You, with relief from Suwad bin Qarib He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed until his molars were visible and said to me: You have succeeded, O Sawad. Umar may God be pleased with him said: Does your opinion come to you now? He said: “Since I recited the Qur’an, it has not come to me. What an excellent compensation is the Book of God from the jinn.” Al-Bayhaqi then narrated it from two other chains of narration. What indicates their delegation to him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after he migrated to Madinah is the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Nu’aym in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, when he said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdah Al-Masisi narrated to us: Abu Tobah Al-Rabi’ ibn Nafi’ narrated to us: Mu’awiyah ibn Salam narrated to us from Zayd ibn Aslam that he heard Abu Salam say: Someone narrated to me from Amr ibn Ghailan Al-Thaqafi: I came to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him and said to him: I was told that you were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. He said: Yes. I said: Tell me how he was! He said: The people of the Suffah, each one of them took a man to feed him, and I was left and none of them took me. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me and said: Who is this? I said: I am Ibn Mas`ud. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did no one take you to feed you? I said: No. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then go, perhaps I will find something for you. He said: So we set off until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to the room of Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her. He left me standing and went in to his family. Then the slave girl came out and said: O Ibn Mas`ud, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not find you dinner, so go back to your bed. He said: So I went back to the mosque and gathered pebbles for the mosque and used them as a pillow and wrapped myself in my garment. I had not stayed long before the slave girl came and said: Answer the Messenger of God. I followed her, hoping for dinner, until I reached my place. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out with a palm frond in his hand and he put it on my chest and said (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Go with me wherever you go. I said: Whatever God wills. He repeated it to me three times. All of that I say, Whatever God wills, so he set out, and I set out with him until we came to Baqi’ al-Gharqad. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line with his staff and then said, Sit in it and do not move until I come to you. Then he set out walking and I was looking at him through the palm trees, until when he was from where I could not see him, a black cloud rose before him and it dispersed. I said, “Catch up with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for I think that the Hawazin have plotted against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him. So I hasten to the houses and seek help from the people. Then I remembered that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had advised me not to move from the place I was in. Then I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, striking them with his staff and saying, “Sit,” so they sat until the dawn column was about to split, then they rose up and left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and said, Are you going to sleep after me? I said: No, but I was frightened at first, so much so that I decided to go to the houses and call for help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your stick, and I thought it was the Hawazin who plotted against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him. He said: “If you had left this circle, I would not have been safe from some of them kidnapping you. Did you see anything from them?” I said: I saw black men with white hair, wearing white clothes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Those are a delegation of the jinn of Nasibin. They came to me and asked me for provisions and food, so I gave them every rotten bone, dung or excrement.” I said: What good will that do them? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “They will not find a bone without finding the flesh on it that was on it the day it was eaten, and they will not find any excrement without finding in it the seed that was in it the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself with a bone or dung.” This is a very strange chain of transmission, but it contains an unknown man who was not named. And God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Nu`aym narrated from the hadith of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid: Numayr ibn Zayd al-Qanbar told me. My father told us, Quhafah ibn Rabi`ah told us, al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam may God be pleased with him told me: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Madinah. When he finished, he said: Which of you will follow me to the delegation of the jinn tonight? So the people were silent for three days, then he passed by me and took my hand and I began to walk with him until all the mountains of the city were blocked from us, and we reached a barren land and there were tall men like spears, feeling their clothes from between their legs. When I saw them, a severe tremor overcame me. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud mentioned above, and this is a strange hadith, and God knows best. Concerning the delegations of the jinn, what Al-Hafiz Abu Nu`aym narrated: Abu Muhammad ibn Hibban told us, Abu Al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Ruh told us, Ya`qub Al-Dawraqi told us, Al-Walid ibn Bakir Al-Taimi told us, Husayn ibn Umar told us, Ubayd Al-Maktab told me on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: A group of Abdullah’s companions went out intending to perform Hajj. When they were on a part of the road, they saw a white snake curled up on the road, with the scent of musk emanating from it. I said to my companion: Go on, for I will not leave until I see what happens to this snake. It did not take long for it to die, so I took a white cloth and wrapped it in it, then moved it away from the road, buried it and joined my companions in eating dinner. He said: By God, we were sitting when four women approached from the direction of sunset. One of them said: Who among you buried Amr? We said: Who is Amr? She said: Who among you buried the snake? I said: I did. She said: By God, I have buried a man who fasted and stood up in prayer, enjoining what God revealed. He believed in your Prophet and heard his description from the heavens four hundred years before he was sent. The man said: So we praised God and completed our Hajj. Then I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him in Madinah and informed him about the snake. He said: You have spoken the truth. I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: He believed in me four hundred years before I was sent. This is a very strange hadith, and God knows best. Abu Nu`aym said: Al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq from Al-Sha`bi from a man from Thaqif in a similar manner. Abdullah bin Ahmad and Al-Dhahrani narrated from Safwan bin Al-Mu`attal: He is the one who descended and buried that snake from among the Companions, and they said that he was the last of the nine to die who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to listen to the Qur’an. Abu Nu`aym narrated from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Sa`d from Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Salamah Al-Majshun from his uncle, from Mu`adh bin Ubayd God bin Mu`ammar, who said: I was sitting with Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, when a man came and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I was in a deserted area. He mentioned that he saw two snakes fighting, then one of them killed the other. He said: So I went to the battlefield and found many snakes that had been killed, and from some of them came the scent of musk. I began to smell them one by one until I found that from a thin yellow snake, so I wrapped it in my turban and buried it. While I was walking, a caller called to me: O Abdullah, you have been guided. These are two tribes of the jinn, Banu Shu'ayban and Banu Qays met, and among those killed were what you saw. The one I buried was martyred, and he was among those who heard the revelation from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman said to that man, "If you are truthful, then you have seen something wondrous. But if you are lying, then your lie will be upon you." And the words of God, the Most High, "And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. Then, when they attended it, they said, 'Listen quietly.'" That is, listen. This was good manners on their part. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi said: Imam Abu Al-Tayyib Sahl bin Muhammad bin Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Daqqaq narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bushanji narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar Al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surah Ar-Rahman until he finished it, then he said: Why do I see you silent? The jinn were better at responding than you. I did not recite this verse to them once: ‘Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?’ except that they said: ‘Nor do we deny any of Your favors and blessings, our Lord, to You be praise.’” At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Waqid, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to his companions and recited to them Surah Ar-Rahman, and he mentioned it. Then At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange. We do not know it except from the hadith of Al-Walid on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, with a similar chain of transmission. God the Almighty said: And when it is concluded meaning completed, as in His saying: So when the prayer is concluded "Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days So when you have completed your rites and they turned back to their people as warners" meaning they returned to their people and warned them of what they heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), as in His saying: "That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they may beware" This verse has been used as evidence that there are warners among the jinn and not messengers, and there is no doubt that God did not send a messenger from among the jinn, as God the Almighty said: "And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns" (10:11). And God the Almighty said: "And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets" (11:11). And He said about Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon him: "And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book" (11:11). So every prophet that God the Almighty sent after Abraham was from his descendants and lineage. As for His saying, the Blessed and Most High, in al-An’am 6:O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? What is meant here is the sum of the two genders, so it applies to one of them, which is mankind, as in His saying: From them come forth pearls and coral, meaning one of them. Then the Almighty explained the warning of the jinn to their people, saying, informing about them: They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a book revealed after Moses.’ They did not mention Jesus because the Gospel was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, in which there were sermons and encouragements and a little of what was permissible and forbidden. In reality, it is like a complement to the Torah, so the Torah is the main body, so that is why they said it was revealed after Moses. This is what Waraqa ibn Nawfal said when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told him the story of Gabriel’s descent, peace be upon him, for the first time, and he said: “Bravo, bravo! This is the law that used to come to Moses. Would that I were a part of it.” Confirming what was before it meaning in the books revealed to the prophets before him. His statement, guides to the truth meaning in belief and information, and to a straight path in actions, for the Qur’an contains two things: information and a request. Its information is truth and its request is justice, as God Almighty said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. And the Almighty said: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. Guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Thus, the jinn said, He guides to the truth in beliefs, and to a straight path, meaning in actions. O our people, respond to the caller of God. This indicates that the Almighty sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to the two groups, the jinn and mankind, where he called them to God the Almighty and recited to them the surah in which the two groups were addressed, charged, and threatened, which is Surat Al-Rahman. For this reason, He said: Respond to the caller of God and believe in him. And the Almighty’s saying: He will forgive you some of your sins. It was said that from here is redundant, and there is consideration in this because its redundancy in affirmation is rare. It was said that it is in its place for partiality. And protect you from a painful punishment, meaning He will save you from His painful punishment. This verse was used as evidence by those scholars who believed that the believing jinn will not enter Paradise, but rather the reward of their righteous ones is that they will be protected from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason, they said this in this context, which is a context of boasting. Exaggeration, if they had a higher reward for faith than this, they would have mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: I was told by Jarir, by Laith, by Mujahid, by Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The believing jinn will not enter Paradise because they are from the offspring of Satan, and the offspring of Satan will not enter Paradise. The truth is that their believers will enter Paradise like the believing humans, as is the doctrine of a group of the Salaf. Some of them used as evidence for this the words of God Almighty: No man or jinn has touched them before them. This evidence is questionable, and better than it is His words, Almighty and Exalted: “And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two Gardens. So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?” God Almighty bestowed His favor upon the two heavy burdens by making the reward of their good-doers Paradise. The jinn responded to this verse with verbal gratitude that was more eloquent than humans, and they said: “And we do not deny any of Your favors, our Lord. To You be praise.” God Almighty would not bestow a favor upon them with a reward that they would not attain. Also, if He were to reward their unbelievers with the Fire, which is a position of justice, then it would be more appropriate for Him to reward their believers with Paradise, which is a position of excellence. This is also indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging, and other similar verses. This issue has been devoted to a separate section, praise and thanks be to God. Paradise will continue to have grace, for which God will create people. Will not those who believe in Him and do good deeds inhabit it? What they have mentioned here about the reward for faith, such as expiation of sins and protection from painful torment, necessitates entering Paradise, because in the Hereafter there is nothing but Paradise and Hellfire. Whoever is protected from Hellfire will inevitably enter Paradise. We do not have any explicit or apparent text from the Shari’ah that says that the believing jinn will not enter Paradise, even if they are protected from Hellfire. If it were true, we would have accepted it, and God knows best. And this is Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his al-Nas 114:He will forgive you your sins and delay you for a specified term. There is no dispute that the believers of his people are in Paradise, and so are these people. Strange sayings have been reported about them. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz may God be pleased with him that they will not enter the spaciousness of Paradise, but will be in its outskirts, its surroundings, and its corners. Some people claim that in Paradise the children of Adam will see them, but they will not see the children of Adam, unlike what happened in this world. Some people say that they will neither eat nor drink in Paradise, but will be inspired with glorification, praise, and sanctification instead of food and drink, like the angels, because they are of the same kind. All of these statements are questionable and have no evidence. Then he said, informing them about them, And whoever does not respond to the caller of God will not escape Him on earth, meaning, God’s power is all-encompassing and encompassing him. And he has no protectors besides Him, meaning, no one can protect them from Him. Those are in manifest error. This is a position of threat and intimidation, so they called their people by encouragement and intimidation, and for this reason it was effective with many of them, and they came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in delegations, as explained above. Praise and thanks be to God, and God knows best.
46:32: Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Abi Za'idah, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi, on the authority of Alqamah, who said: I said to Abdullah bin Mas'ud may God be pleased with him: Did any of you accompany the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Night of the Jinn? He said: None of us accompanied him, but we missed him one night in Mecca, so we said: Was he assassinated? Blown away? What did he do? He said: So we spent the worst night that a people had spent. When it was the break of dawn - or he said - in the early hours of the morning, we saw him coming from the direction of Hira. We said: O Messenger of God, and they mentioned to him what they had been through. He said: A caller of the jinn came to me, so I went to them and recited to them. He said: So he went and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. Al-Sha’bi said: They asked him for provisions. Aamer said: They asked him in Mecca and they were from the jinn of the peninsula. He said: Every bone on which the name of God has been mentioned that falls into your hands will have more meat, and every dung or excrement is fodder for your animals. He said: Do not use them for cleaning yourself, for they are the provisions of your brothers from the jinn. Muslim narrated it in this way in his Sahih on the authority of Ali ibn Hujr on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah with a similar wording. Muslim also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud - who is Ibn Abi Hind - told us on the authority of Amir, who said: I asked Alqamah: Was Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him present with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Night of the Jinn? Alqamah said: I asked Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him and said: Was any of you present with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Night of the Jinn? He said: No, but we were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one night and we missed him. We looked for him in the valleys and ravines, and it was said: Was he taken captive? Was he assassinated? He said: So we spent the worst night ever spent by any people. When morning came, he came from the direction of Hira. He said: We said: O Messenger of God, we missed you and looked for you but did not find you. We spent the worst night ever spent by any people. He said: A caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with them and recited the Qur’an to them. He said: So he set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. They asked him for provisions, and he said: Every bone on which the name of God has been mentioned that falls into your hands will have more meat, and every dung or excrement will be fodder for your animals. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not use them for cleaning yourself, for they are the food of your brothers. Another chain of transmission On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Ahmad bin Abd al-Rahman told me, my uncle told me, Yunus told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abdullah, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I spent the night reciting to the jinn while standing in al-Hujun. Another chain of transmission states that he was with him on the night of the jinn. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, my uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Uthman ibn Sunnah al-Khuza’i, who was from the people of Ash-Sham, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions while he was in Mecca: Whoever among you would like to be present during the affair of the jinn tonight, let him do so. None of them were present except me. He said: So we set off until we were at the top of Mecca. He drew a line for me with his foot, then ordered me to sit in it. Then he set off until he stood up and began to recite the Qur’an, but a great many black clouds covered him and stood between me and him until I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of clouds, going away until only a group of them remained. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished and gave them bones and dung, then he forbade anyone from using dung or bones to perfume themselves. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Wahb ibn Rashid, on the authority of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, with this chain of transmission. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Al-Dala’il from the hadith of Abdullah bin Saleh, the scribe of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yunus, on his authority. Ishaq bin Rahawayh narrated it from Jarir, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Al-Hafiz Abu Na’im narrated it from the path of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu’alla, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and he also mentioned something similar to it. Another chain of transmission Abu Naim said: Abu Malik told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told me, he said: Affan and Ikrimah told us, they said: Mu’tamir told us, he said: My father told me, Abu Tamima told me, on the authority of Amr, and perhaps al-Bakali said, Amr told him, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed me, so we set out until we came to such and such a place, and he drew a line for me and said: Stay in the back of this place and do not leave it, for if you leave it, you will perish. So he mentioned the hadith in full, and it contains great strangeness. Another chain of transmission Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Ghailan ath-Thaqafi, that he said to Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: I was told that you were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. He said: Yes. He said: How was it? Then he mentioned the hadith and mentioned that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) drew a line over him and said: Do not leave it. Then he mentioned something like a black cloud that overwhelmed the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and he was frightened three times until it was close to dawn. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to me and said: Are you asleep? I said: “No, by God. I thought many times of calling for help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your staff, saying: “Sit down.” Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If you went out, I would not be safe from some of them snatching you away. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Did you see anything? I said: Yes, I saw black men with white hair, wearing white clothes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Those were jinn from Nasibin who asked me for provisions - and provisions are provisions - so I gave them provisions with every loose bone, dung or excrement. I said: O Messenger of God, what will that do for them? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They will not find a bone without finding its flesh on it on the day it was eaten, nor dung without finding its seeds in it on the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself when he comes out of the toilet with a bone, dung or excrement.” Another way Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sammali and Abu Nasr bin Qatada told us, he said: Abu Muhammad bin Yahya bin Mansour Al-Qadi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bushanji told us, Ruh bin Salah told us, Musa bin Ali bin Rabah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a follower and said: A group of fifteen jinn, sons of brothers and cousins, will come to me tonight so that I may recite the Qur’an to them. So I went with him to the place he wanted, and he drew a line for me and made me sit there and said to me: Do not leave this place. So I spent the night there until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me with magic in his hand, a broken bone, dung, and a birthmark, and he said: If you go to the toilet, do not clean yourself with anything of these. He said: When morning came, I said: “I will know where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was.” So I went and saw a place where sixty camels would kneel. Another chain of transmission Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Al-Abbas bin Muhammad Al-Duri informed us, Uthman bin Omar informed us, on the authority of Al-Shammar bin Al-Rayyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: I set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn until we reached Al-Hujun. He drew a line for me, then he advanced towards them, and they crowded around him. A chief of theirs, called Wardan, said: I will make them leave you. He said: No one will protect me from God. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan ibn Abi Fazarah al-Absi told us, Abu Zayd, the freed slave of Amr ibn Harith, told us, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the night of the jinn came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you have water with you? I said: I do not have water with me, but I have a jug of wine with me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A good date and pure water. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Zayd. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Qais ibn al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Hanash al-San’ani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them, who said: He was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the jinn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, do you have water with you? He said: I have wine in a water skin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pour it over me. So he performed ablution. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abdullah, a drink and purification. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this chain of transmission. Ad-Daraqutni included it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, my father told me, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. When he had finished, he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. This is how I saw it in the Musnad in an abbreviated form. Al-Hafiz Abu Nu’aym narrated it in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, and he said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, and Abu Bakr ibn Malik told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, my father told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mina’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Abu Bakr. He was silent, then a while passed, then he sighed, so I said: What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God? He said: My death has been reported to me, O Ibn Mas’ud. I said: Appoint a successor. He said: Who? I said: Umar. He was silent for a while, then he passed away. Then he took a deep breath, so I said, What is the matter with you? He said, My death has been reported to me. I said, Then appoint a successor. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Who? I said, Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if they obey him, they will all enter Paradise, all of them. This is a very strange hadith and it is more likely that it has not been preserved. Assuming its authenticity, it appears that this was after their arrival to him in Medina, as we will mention, God willing. At that time, at the end of the matter, when Mecca was conquered and the people and the jinn also entered the religion of God in multitudes, the Surah “When the help of God and the conquest come, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance” was revealed. This is the Surah in which his noble soul was announced to him, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, stated, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, agreed with him on it. A hadith has been reported about that, which we will mention, God willing, when interpreting it. And God knows best. Abu Nu`aym also narrated it on the authority of Al-Tabari, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Husayn bin Abi Burdah, on the authority of Yahya bin Sa`id Al-Aslami, on the authority of Harb bin Subaih, on the authority of Sa`id bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Murrah Al-San`ani, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Jadali on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, mentioned it and mentioned the story of the succession. This is a strange chain of transmission and a wondrous context. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line around him, and one of them was like the blackness of a palm tree, and he said: Do not move from your place, and teach them the Book of God. When he saw the pasture, he said: They are like these. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you have water with you? I said: No. He said: Do you have wine with you? I said: Yes. So he performed ablution with it. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told us, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, he said: They were twelve thousand who came from the island of Mosul. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him: Give me time until I come to you, and he drew a line over it and said: Do not move until I come to you. When Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, feared them, he was about to leave, but he remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not move. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: If you had left, we would not have met until the Day of Resurrection. Another chain of transmission also transmitted: Sa`id bin Abi `Aruba said on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were directed to him from Nineveh and that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to recite to the jinn, so which of you will follow me? So they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him, and they lowered their gaze, then he asked them to follow him a third time. A man said: O Messenger of God, that is the one with a scar, so Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, the brother of Hudhayl, followed him. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a valley called the Valley of al-Hujun and drew a line over it, and he drew a line over Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, to confirm it. He said: So I began to tremble and I saw things like eagles walking in their tambourines, and I heard a loud noise until I feared for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited the Qur’an, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, I said: O Messenger of God, what was the noise that I heard? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They disputed over a murdered person, and a judgment was passed between them in truth. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. All these methods indicate that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the jinn intentionally, recited the Qur’an to them, called them to God Almighty, and God Almighty prescribed for them through his tongue what they needed at that time. It may be possible that the first time they heard him recite the Qur’an, he did not notice them, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said. Then after that, they came to him, as narrated by Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him. As for Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him, he was not with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he addressed the jinn and called upon them. Rather, he was far away from him, and no one went out with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) except him. Despite this, he did not witness the speech. This is the method of Al-Bayhaqi. It may be possible that the first time he went out to them, neither Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him nor anyone else was with him, as is apparent in the context of the first narration on the authority of Imam Ahmad, which is in Muslim. Then after that, he went out with him another night, and God knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his interpretation of Say, ‘It has been revealed to me’ from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: `Abd Al-`Aziz ibn `Umar said: As for the jinn whom they met at Nakhlah, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn whom they met in Mecca, they were the jinn of Nasibin. Al-Bayhaqi interpreted it as meaning that he said, “We spent the worst night that a people spent, other than Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him who did not know about his (blessings and peace of God be upon him) going out to the jinn.” This is a remote possibility, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Amr Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Adeeb told us, Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili told us, Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Amr bin Yahya told us, on the authority of his grandfather Saeed bin Amr, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, used to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a vessel for his ablution and for his needs. One day he caught up with him and said, Who is this? He said, I am Abu Hurairah. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Bring me stones to clean myself with, but do not bring me bones or dung. So I brought him stones in my garment and placed them beside him. When he had finished and stood up, I followed him and said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with bones and dung? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A delegation of the jinn of Nasibin came to me and asked me for provisions, so I supplicated to God for them that they would not pass by a bone or dung without finding it to be food. Narrated by Al-Bukhari in his Sahih on the authority of Musa ibn Isma’il on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya with a similar chain of transmission. This indicates what was mentioned above, that they came to him after that, and we will mention, God willing, what indicates the repetition of that. Ibn Abbas narrated other narrations than what was narrated from him at first, from a new chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani narrated to us, Al-Nadr bin Arabi narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the verse: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed them as messengers to their people. This indicates that he narrated both stories. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein narrated to us, Suwaid bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, a man whom he named, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: {And when We directed to you a company of the jinn} (Al-Araf: 14), he said: They were seven men, three from the people of Harran and four from the people of Nasibin, and their names were Huyy, Hasi, Mansa, Sasir, Nasir, Al-Ardubian, and Al-Ahtam. Abu Hamza Al-Thamali mentioned that this clan of jinn was called Banu Al-Shisaan, and they were the most numerous and noblest of the jinn, and they were the majority of Satan’s soldiers. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, that they were nine, one of them was Zuba`ah. They came to him from the base of a palm tree. It was mentioned earlier that they were fifteen, and in a narration that they were on sixty camels. It was mentioned earlier that the name of their master was Wardan, and it was said that they were three hundred. It was mentioned earlier on the authority of `Ikrimah that they were twelve thousand. Perhaps this difference is evidence of the repetition of their delegation to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. What indicates that is what al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn Wahb told me, `Umar told me, he is Ibn Muhammad, he said: Salim told him, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I never heard `Umar, may God be pleased with him, say anything, I think it is like this, except that it was as he thought. While `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was sitting, a handsome man passed by him and he said: My assumption was wrong, or This man is following his religion in the pre-Islamic period, or “He was their soothsayer. Bring me the man.” So he was summoned, and he said that to him. He said: I have never seen a Muslim man like today. He said: I urge you to do nothing but tell me. He said: I was… Their priest in the pre-Islamic period said: How strange is what your jinn brought you? He said: While I was in the market one day, she came to me and I knew she was frightened, and she said: Have you not seen the jinn and their despair and hopelessness after their defeat? And its pursuit of the camels and their saddles Umar may God be pleased with him said: He spoke the truth while I was sleeping beside their gods when a man came with a calf and slaughtered it. A caller cried out over it in a voice I had never heard a louder than his, saying: O Jalih, the order of Nujayh is an eloquent man who says: There is no god but God. The people jumped up and I said: I will not leave until I know what is behind this. Then he called: O Jalih, the order of Nujayh is an eloquent man who says: There is no god but God. I got up and it was not long before it was said: This is a prophet. This is the context of Bukhari. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb in a similar manner. Then he said: The apparent meaning of this narration suggests that Umar may God be pleased with him himself heard the caller crying out from the slaughtered calf. This is also clear in a weak narration from Umar may God be pleased with him. All the other narrations indicate that this soothsayer is the one who reported that he saw and heard it. And God knows best. What Al-Bayhaqi said is the correct one and this man is Sawad ibn Qarib. I have mentioned this in detail in the biography of Umar may God be pleased with him, so whoever wants it can take it from there. Praise and gratitude be to God. Al-Bayhaqi said: The hadith of Sawad bin Qarib, and it is likely that this is the soothsayer whose name was not mentioned in the authentic hadith, Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Habib al-Mufassir told us from the original hearing, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Asbahani told us, reading to him, Abu Ja`far Ahmad bin Musa al-Himar al-Kufi told us in Kufa, Ziyad bin Yazid bin Badawayh told us, Abu Bakr al-Qasri told us, Muhammad bin al-Nawwas al-Kufi told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara` may God be pleased with him, who said: While `Umar bin al-Khattab may God be pleased with him was delivering a sermon to the people on the pulpit of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said: O people, is Sawad bin Qarib among you? He said: No one answered him that year. Then the following year came, he said: O people, is Sawad bin Qarib among you? I said: O Commander of the Faithful, and who is Sawad bin Qarib? He said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said to him: The beginning of Sawad bin Qarib’s conversion to Islam was something amazing. He said: While we were like that, Sawad bin Qarib appeared. He said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said to him: O Sawad, tell us about the beginning of your conversion to Islam, how was it? Sawad, may God be pleased with him, said: I was staying in India and I had a vision from the jinn. He said: While I was sleeping one night, that came to me in my dream. He said: Get up and understand and reason if you can reason. A messenger has been sent from Lu’ay bin Ghalib. Then he began to say: I was amazed at the jinn and their feelings, and the camels’ attraction to their saddles. You go to Mecca seeking guidance. The jinn are not as good as its filth. Rise up to the elite of Hashim and look up to her head He said: Then he woke me up and startled me and said, O Sawad bin Qarib, God Almighty has sent a prophet, so rise up to him and you will be guided and be given the right direction. Then, on the second night, he came to me and woke me up and then began to say: I was amazed at the jinn and their demands, and the camels pulling them with their saddlebags. She heads to Mecca seeking guidance, her feet not like her tails Rise up to the elite of Hashim and look up to its summit Then, on the third night, he came to me, woke me up, and said: I was amazed at the jinn and their stories, and the camels pulling them with their camels She goes to Mecca seeking guidance. The evil ones are not like the good ones. Rise up to the elite of Hashim. The believers of the jinn are not like their disbelievers. He said: When I heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam, through the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell into my heart as God willed. He said: So I went to my saddlebag and tied it to my mount. I did not undo nine knots or tie another knot until I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and behold, he was in Medina, meaning Mecca, and the people were upon him like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw me, he said: “Welcome, O Sawad bin Qarib. We know what brought you.” He said: I said, O Messenger of God, I have recited poetry, so hear it from me. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say, O Sawad. So I said: A vision came to me after a long night of sleep, and it was not a liar among what I have been tested with. Three nights, saying every night: A messenger from Luay ibn Ghalib has come to you. So I rolled up my trousers and the foxes walked between the two sides of the river. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are trustworthy with all who are absent. You are the closest of the messengers to intercede with God, O son of the most noble and good. So command us to do what comes to you, O best messenger, even if what comes is gray hair. And be my intercessor on the day when there is no intercessor but You, with relief from Suwad bin Qarib He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed until his molars were visible and said to me: You have succeeded, O Sawad. Umar may God be pleased with him said: Does your opinion come to you now? He said: “Since I recited the Qur’an, it has not come to me. What an excellent compensation is the Book of God from the jinn.” Al-Bayhaqi then narrated it from two other chains of narration. What indicates their delegation to him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after he migrated to Madinah is the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Nu’aym in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, when he said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdah Al-Masisi narrated to us: Abu Tobah Al-Rabi’ ibn Nafi’ narrated to us: Mu’awiyah ibn Salam narrated to us from Zayd ibn Aslam that he heard Abu Salam say: Someone narrated to me from Amr ibn Ghailan Al-Thaqafi: I came to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him and said to him: I was told that you were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of the delegation of the jinn. He said: Yes. I said: Tell me how he was! He said: The people of the Suffah, each one of them took a man to feed him, and I was left and none of them took me. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me and said: Who is this? I said: I am Ibn Mas`ud. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did no one take you to feed you? I said: No. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then go, perhaps I will find something for you. He said: So we set off until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to the room of Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her. He left me standing and went in to his family. Then the slave girl came out and said: O Ibn Mas`ud, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not find you dinner, so go back to your bed. He said: So I went back to the mosque and gathered pebbles for the mosque and used them as a pillow and wrapped myself in my garment. I had not stayed long before the slave girl came and said: Answer the Messenger of God. I followed her, hoping for dinner, until I reached my place. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out with a palm frond in his hand and he put it on my chest and said (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Go with me wherever you go. I said: Whatever God wills. He repeated it to me three times. All of that I say, Whatever God wills, so he set out, and I set out with him until we came to Baqi’ al-Gharqad. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line with his staff and then said, Sit in it and do not move until I come to you. Then he set out walking and I was looking at him through the palm trees, until when he was from where I could not see him, a black cloud rose before him and it dispersed. I said, “Catch up with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for I think that the Hawazin have plotted against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him. So I hasten to the houses and seek help from the people. Then I remembered that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had advised me not to move from the place I was in. Then I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, striking them with his staff and saying, “Sit,” so they sat until the dawn column was about to split, then they rose up and left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and said, Are you going to sleep after me? I said: No, but I was frightened at first, so much so that I decided to go to the houses and call for help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your stick, and I thought it was the Hawazin who plotted against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him. He said: “If you had left this circle, I would not have been safe from some of them kidnapping you. Did you see anything from them?” I said: I saw black men with white hair, wearing white clothes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Those are a delegation of the jinn of Nasibin. They came to me and asked me for provisions and food, so I gave them every rotten bone, dung or excrement.” I said: What good will that do them? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “They will not find a bone without finding the flesh on it that was on it the day it was eaten, and they will not find any excrement without finding in it the seed that was in it the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself with a bone or dung.” This is a very strange chain of transmission, but it contains an unknown man who was not named. And God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Nu`aym narrated from the hadith of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid: Numayr ibn Zayd al-Qanbar told me. My father told us, Quhafah ibn Rabi`ah told us, al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam may God be pleased with him told me: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Madinah. When he finished, he said: Which of you will follow me to the delegation of the jinn tonight? So the people were silent for three days, then he passed by me and took my hand and I began to walk with him until all the mountains of the city were blocked from us, and we reached a barren land and there were tall men like spears, feeling their clothes from between their legs. When I saw them, a severe tremor overcame me. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud mentioned above, and this is a strange hadith, and God knows best. Concerning the delegations of the jinn, what Al-Hafiz Abu Nu`aym narrated: Abu Muhammad ibn Hibban told us, Abu Al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Ruh told us, Ya`qub Al-Dawraqi told us, Al-Walid ibn Bakir Al-Taimi told us, Husayn ibn Umar told us, Ubayd Al-Maktab told me on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: A group of Abdullah’s companions went out intending to perform Hajj. When they were on a part of the road, they saw a white snake curled up on the road, with the scent of musk emanating from it. I said to my companion: Go on, for I will not leave until I see what happens to this snake. It did not take long for it to die, so I took a white cloth and wrapped it in it, then moved it away from the road, buried it and joined my companions in eating dinner. He said: By God, we were sitting when four women approached from the direction of sunset. One of them said: Who among you buried Amr? We said: Who is Amr? She said: Who among you buried the snake? I said: I did. She said: By God, I have buried a man who fasted and stood up in prayer, enjoining what God revealed. He believed in your Prophet and heard his description from the heavens four hundred years before he was sent. The man said: So we praised God and completed our Hajj. Then I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him in Madinah and informed him about the snake. He said: You have spoken the truth. I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: He believed in me four hundred years before I was sent. This is a very strange hadith, and God knows best. Abu Nu`aym said: Al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq from Al-Sha`bi from a man from Thaqif in a similar manner. Abdullah bin Ahmad and Al-Dhahrani narrated from Safwan bin Al-Mu`attal: He is the one who descended and buried that snake from among the Companions, and they said that he was the last of the nine to die who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to listen to the Qur’an. Abu Nu`aym narrated from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Sa`d from Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Salamah Al-Majshun from his uncle, from Mu`adh bin Ubayd God bin Mu`ammar, who said: I was sitting with Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, when a man came and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I was in a deserted area. He mentioned that he saw two snakes fighting, then one of them killed the other. He said: So I went to the battlefield and found many snakes that had been killed, and from some of them came the scent of musk. I began to smell them one by one until I found that from a thin yellow snake, so I wrapped it in my turban and buried it. While I was walking, a caller called to me: O Abdullah, you have been guided. These are two tribes of the jinn, Banu Shu'ayban and Banu Qays met, and among those killed were what you saw. The one I buried was martyred, and he was among those who heard the revelation from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman said to that man, "If you are truthful, then you have seen something wondrous. But if you are lying, then your lie will be upon you." And the words of God, the Most High, "And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. Then, when they attended it, they said, 'Listen quietly.'" That is, listen. This was good manners on their part. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi said: Imam Abu Al-Tayyib Sahl bin Muhammad bin Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Daqqaq narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Bushanji narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar Al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surah Ar-Rahman until he finished it, then he said: Why do I see you silent? The jinn were better at responding than you. I did not recite this verse to them once: ‘Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?’ except that they said: ‘Nor do we deny any of Your favors and blessings, our Lord, to You be praise.’” At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Waqid, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to his companions and recited to them Surah Ar-Rahman, and he mentioned it. Then At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange. We do not know it except from the hadith of Al-Walid on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, with a similar chain of transmission.
