God the Almighty said: And when it is concluded meaning completed, as in His saying: So when the prayer is concluded "Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days So when you have completed your rites and they turned back to their people as warners" meaning they returned to their people and warned them of what they heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), as in His saying: "That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they may beware" This verse has been used as evidence that there are warners among the jinn and not messengers, and there is no doubt that God did not send a messenger from among the jinn, as God the Almighty said: "And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns" (10:11). And God the Almighty said: "And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets" (11:11). And He said about Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon him: "And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book" (11:11). So every prophet that God the Almighty sent after Abraham was from his descendants and lineage. As for His saying, the Blessed and Most High, in al-An’am 6:O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? What is meant here is the sum of the two genders, so it applies to one of them, which is mankind, as in His saying: From them come forth pearls and coral, meaning one of them. Then the Almighty explained the warning of the jinn to their people, saying, informing about them: They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a book revealed after Moses.’ They did not mention Jesus because the Gospel was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, in which there were sermons and encouragements and a little of what was permissible and forbidden. In reality, it is like a complement to the Torah, so the Torah is the main body, so that is why they said it was revealed after Moses. This is what Waraqa ibn Nawfal said when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told him the story of Gabriel’s descent, peace be upon him, for the first time, and he said: “Bravo, bravo! This is the law that used to come to Moses. Would that I were a part of it.” Confirming what was before it meaning in the books revealed to the prophets before him. His statement, guides to the truth meaning in belief and information, and to a straight path in actions, for the Qur’an contains two things: information and a request. Its information is truth and its request is justice, as God Almighty said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. And the Almighty said: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. Guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Thus, the jinn said, He guides to the truth in beliefs, and to a straight path, meaning in actions. O our people, respond to the caller of God. This indicates that the Almighty sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to the two groups, the jinn and mankind, where he called them to God the Almighty and recited to them the surah in which the two groups were addressed, charged, and threatened, which is Surat Al-Rahman. For this reason, He said: Respond to the caller of God and believe in him. And the Almighty’s saying: He will forgive you some of your sins. It was said that from here is redundant, and there is consideration in this because its redundancy in affirmation is rare. It was said that it is in its place for partiality. And protect you from a painful punishment, meaning He will save you from His painful punishment. This verse was used as evidence by those scholars who believed that the believing jinn will not enter Paradise, but rather the reward of their righteous ones is that they will be protected from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason, they said this in this context, which is a context of boasting. Exaggeration, if they had a higher reward for faith than this, they would have mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: I was told by Jarir, by Laith, by Mujahid, by Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The believing jinn will not enter Paradise because they are from the offspring of Satan, and the offspring of Satan will not enter Paradise. The truth is that their believers will enter Paradise like the believing humans, as is the doctrine of a group of the Salaf. Some of them used as evidence for this the words of God Almighty: No man or jinn has touched them before them. This evidence is questionable, and better than it is His words, Almighty and Exalted: “And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two Gardens. So which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?” God Almighty bestowed His favor upon the two heavy burdens by making the reward of their good-doers Paradise. The jinn responded to this verse with verbal gratitude that was more eloquent than humans, and they said: “And we do not deny any of Your favors, our Lord. To You be praise.” God Almighty would not bestow a favor upon them with a reward that they would not attain. Also, if He were to reward their unbelievers with the Fire, which is a position of justice, then it would be more appropriate for Him to reward their believers with Paradise, which is a position of excellence. This is also indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging, and other similar verses. This issue has been devoted to a separate section, praise and thanks be to God. Paradise will continue to have grace, for which God will create people. Will not those who believe in Him and do good deeds inhabit it? What they have mentioned here about the reward for faith, such as expiation of sins and protection from painful torment, necessitates entering Paradise, because in the Hereafter there is nothing but Paradise and Hellfire. Whoever is protected from Hellfire will inevitably enter Paradise. We do not have any explicit or apparent text from the Shari’ah that says that the believing jinn will not enter Paradise, even if they are protected from Hellfire. If it were true, we would have accepted it, and God knows best. And this is Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his al-Nas 114:He will forgive you your sins and delay you for a specified term. There is no dispute that the believers of his people are in Paradise, and so are these people. Strange sayings have been reported about them. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz may God be pleased with him that they will not enter the spaciousness of Paradise, but will be in its outskirts, its surroundings, and its corners. Some people claim that in Paradise the children of Adam will see them, but they will not see the children of Adam, unlike what happened in this world. Some people say that they will neither eat nor drink in Paradise, but will be inspired with glorification, praise, and sanctification instead of food and drink, like the angels, because they are of the same kind. All of these statements are questionable and have no evidence. Then he said, informing them about them, And whoever does not respond to the caller of God will not escape Him on earth, meaning, God’s power is all-encompassing and encompassing him. And he has no protectors besides Him, meaning, no one can protect them from Him. Those are in manifest error. This is a position of threat and intimidation, so they called their people by encouragement and intimidation, and for this reason it was effective with many of them, and they came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in delegations, as explained above. Praise and thanks be to God, and God knows best.
46:33: God the Almighty says: Have these deniers of the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, who reject the resurrection of bodies on the Day of Judgment, not seen that God is He who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary of their creation, that is, He did not make their creation difficult for Him, but rather said to them, Be, and they were, without resistance or opposition, but rather obedient, responsive, and fearful. Is He not able to bring the dead to life? As God the Almighty said in another verse: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know. For this reason God the Almighty said: Yes, He is over all things competent. Then the Almighty said, threatening and warning those who disbelieved in Him, And on the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, Is this not the truth? It will be said to them, Is this not the truth? Is this magic, or do you not see? They said, Yes, by our Lord." That is, they could not do anything but confess. "He said, 'Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.'" Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient over the denial of those among his people who denied him: "So be patient as were patient the messengers of strong will." There are different opinions regarding the number of those of strong will, the most well-known of which are that they are Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God, the Most High, has mentioned their names from among the prophets in two verses in Surat Al-Ahzab and Surat Ash-Shura. It may be possible that what is meant by those of strong will is all the messengers, so the word "of in His statement, of the messengers," is to indicate the type, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Hadrami told us, al-Sarri ibn Hayyan told us, Ibad ibn Ibad told us, Mujalid ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fasted for a long time, then he continued fasting for a long time, then he continued fasting for a long time, then he said: O Aisha, this world is not suitable for Muhammad or the family of Muhammad. O Aisha, God Almighty was not pleased with the messengers of strong will except with patience in what is disliked and patience in what is beloved to them. Then He was not pleased with me except to charge me with what He charged them with, so He said: ‘So be patient as the messengers of strong will were patient.’ And by God, I will be patient as they were patient to the best of my ability. There is no strength except with God. ‘And do not hasten for them,’ meaning do not hasten for them the punishment to come upon them, as God Almighty says: ‘And leave Me and the deniers, those of wealth, and grant them respite for a little.’ And as God Almighty says: ‘So grant respite to the disbelievers. Grant them respite for a little while.’ ‘As if, on the Day they see what they are promised, “They did not remain except for an hour of a day.” As in the words of God, the Most High: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained except for an afternoon or a morning thereof. And as in the words of God, the Most High: And the Day He gathers them together, it will be as if they had not remained except for an hour of a day; they will recognize one another. And the words of God, the Most High: A message. Ibn Jarir said that it has two possible meanings: One of them is that it is understood to mean, That is a message, and the other is that it is understood to mean, This Qur’an is a message. And the words of God, the Most High: Then are none destroyed except the wicked people? Meaning, none is destroyed by God except those who are destroyed. This is from His justice, the Most High, that He does not punish anyone except those who deserve punishment, and God knows best.
